slots.label: Heading 1
slots.default: Your backup is a target, not a safety net

slots.label: Paragraph 1
slots.default: Ransomware crews worked out years ago that encrypting live data is only half a job. If the victim can restore, they do not pay. So the backups get attacked first, and the tools people rely on most are the ones sitting on the same network with the same administrator credentials.

slots.label: Paragraph 2
slots.default: At least one copy has to be somewhere the attacker cannot touch. Immutable storage that cannot be altered or deleted for a set period, separate credentials that are not the ones your domain admin uses daily, and multi-factor authentication on the backup console itself. The old three copies, two media, one offsite rule still holds up, with the modern addition that one copy should be genuinely unchangeable.

slots.label: Paragraph 3
slots.default: Attackers commonly sit inside a network for weeks before triggering anything. If your retention is short, your clean restore point may already have been deleted by the time you need it. Retention is a security decision, not just a storage cost.
